unit: B3-B (backend) Sign in with Apple token revocation, dark flag ENABLE_APPLE_TOKEN_REVOCATION. Worktree C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s79-b3revoke, branch feature/s79-b3-apple-revoke, GREEN commit e8f11873 (parent b965c63b).
lens: sec (secrets / security adversary). Scope: private key handling, every [SIWA] log line, the refresh token at rest (044), client_secret JWT shape, OpenAPI limit, bounded timeouts, retry storms, CREDENTIALS_UNSET, test-file literals, gitleaks, bundle ids, and whether any failure can block account deletion.

findings.title: Pin gap: a non-transport exception in the revoke can be re-raised into delete_user_account and no frozen test notices, so it would block the auth delete
findings.evidence: Mutant S23 in revoke_refresh_token changes `continue / return False` to `continue / raise` (the except arm for exceptions that are not httpx.HTTPError or TimeoutError). It SURVIVED: 102 passed, [pyt] 14:06:07-14:06:19 12s status=OK rc=0. R14 only covers ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout and status codes. The current bytes are correct: probe B test_p3 (the transport raises a non-httpx TypeError) gives deletion True, auth_delete once and 1 attempt; test_p2 (admin.table raises TypeError, RuntimeError, KeyError or AttributeError) also gives deletion True. [pyt] tag=b3b-adv-sec-probeB 13:51:40-13:52:04 status=OK, 30 passed. The call site `await apple_siwa_service.revoke_refresh_token(siwa_token)` in auth_service.delete_user_account has no belt of its own, so a future regression inside the revoke would leave the cascade done and the auth user alive (500).
findings.fix: Add an R14 param whose transport raises a non-httpx exception (for example a RuntimeError subclass built without the request kwarg). It should give 1 attempt, `revoke attempt=1 failed: <Type>`, deletion True and auth_delete once. This kills S23 and S7. Optionally also wrap the call site in try/except Exception with one WARNING `[SIWA] revoke failed: <Type>`.

findings.title: Pin gap: the `[SIWA] revoke attempt=%d failed` line can move to ERROR with exc_info and no test notices (X31 holds only for the lines R18 replays)
findings.evidence: Mutant S4 (logger.warning becomes logger.error(..., exc_info=True) on the revoke-failure line) SURVIVED: 102 passed, [pyt] 13:57:25-13:57:30 5s status=OK rc=0. R14 compares `_siwa_lines(logs)` with no level filter. R18 replays only the revoke 200 and 503x2 paths, and the R8 AST pin skips except arms. The same mutant on the other WARNING lines IS killed by the level-filtered rows R9, R15 and R27: S4b, S4c, S4d and S4e all KILLED. If this regressed, an ERROR record would become a Sentry event through LoggingIntegration. Exposure would stay limited: include_local_variables=False (sentry_service.py:681) and U8d blanks exception values.
findings.fix: In R14, assert the non-200 lines with `_siwa_lines(logs, logging.WARNING)`. Alternatively, add a revoke transport-failure scenario (ConnectTimeout then 200) to the R18 replay so its level / exc_info / template checks cover the `failed:` template.

findings.title: Pin gap: disabling TLS verification on the Apple client (verify=False) passes every test
findings.evidence: Mutant S5 (`httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=_HTTP_TIMEOUT, transport=_TRANSPORT, verify=False)`) SURVIVED: 102 passed, [pyt] 13:57:30-13:57:45 15s status=OK rc=0. MockTransport ignores TLS. The current code verifies through the httpx default, and with _TRANSPORT None the real transport was exercised in probe A over loopback. Such a regression would send the client_secret, the authorization code and the refresh token over an unverified channel.
findings.fix: Add a static pin, an AST scan of apple_siwa_service.py, asserting that every httpx.AsyncClient(...) call takes only the keywords {timeout, transport}: no verify, trust_env or proxy. Also assert that _TRANSPORT is None at import.

findings.title: Pin gap on GB5: nothing checks that key material stays out of exception messages
findings.evidence: Mutant S3 (`raise ValueError("unparseable private key: " + text) from None`) SURVIVED: 102 passed, [pyt] 13:56:52-13:57:24 32s status=OK rc=0. R9[garbage-key] only checks the log line, which logs the type name. The current bytes are clean: probe A built 17 key forms (real / literal-\n / base64 / base64 wrapped at 76 / CRLF / quoted / SEC1 / truncated / garbage body / P-384 / RSA / public / encrypted / base64 of garbage / base64 of text / bare body / spaces) and checked str, repr, args and the __context__ chain. 0 LEAK; the types were ValueError / InvalidKeyError / AttributeError / TypeError. The exceptions are swallowed with the type logged only, so there is no exposure today.
findings.fix: In R3 (garbage and RSA) or R9[garbage-key], also call siwa._normalise_private_key / build_client_secret directly and assert that no PEM body line appears in str(exc) + repr(exc).

findings.title: The revoke retries on any exception type, against the spec's transport/timeout-only rule; still bounded at 2, so no storm
findings.evidence: Mutant S7 (`if isinstance(exc, (httpx.HTTPError, asyncio.TimeoutError)):` becomes `if True:`) SURVIVED: [pyt] 13:59:01-13:59:16 status=OK. Probe A attempt counts on the current bytes: 200:1, 400:1, 401:1, 500->200:2, 503x2:2, 429x2:2, ConnectError x3:2, RuntimeError:1, OSError:1. The exchange is single shot on 400 / 429 / 500 / ConnectError / RuntimeError.
findings.fix: Closed by the same R14 param as SEC-1.

findings.title: Operational: a mis-pasted key fails soft and silently voids revocation
findings.evidence: In probe A, a PEM wrapped in quotes gives ValueError; an encrypted PKCS#8 gives TypeError; a public-key PEM gives AttributeError; a P-384 or RSA key gives InvalidKeyError. Each logs only `[SIWA] client secret build failed: <Type>` and sends no request. The B4 canary (`exchange status=200`, `stored`) is the only detector.
findings.fix: In the owner step / CLAUDE.md row, add one line: paste the .p8 without surrounding quotes, and treat any `client secret build failed` line during the canary as a stop.

findings.title: authorization_code has no length cap, by design (X34), and any length is forwarded to Apple once per successful Apple sign-in while the flag is ON
findings.evidence: auth_routes.SocialLoginRequest.authorization_code is Optional[str] with no max_length (ruling Q11 / X34). The exchange runs only after Supabase verified the Apple id_token and the 401 / consent raises (R25). The route is limited to 10/minute. Probe P7: the 422 paths (bad provider, missing id_token, 40-char terms_version) neither echo nor log the code.
findings.fix: Optional: in store_apple_refresh_token, skip the exchange when len(authorization_code) > 4096. This keeps the model and the flag-OFF identity unchanged.

findings.title: Accepted design windows: up to 12 s between the cascade and the auth delete, and a concurrent sign-in between the read and the auth delete stores a token that is never revoked
findings.evidence: Probe B test_p4: a hung revoke at the real _CALL_DEADLINE gives elapsed=12.00s, attempts=2, then the auth delete runs. Spec 2.5 / L7 accept crash safety (a retry reads the row again). The read happens before the cascade, so an upsert landing after the read is replaced by nothing and its row is dropped by the FK cascade, leaving that Apple link active. That needs the same user to sign in during their own deletion.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally record it as a stated limit beside L7.

findings.title: Observed during mutation: the unhandled-exception handler logs the raw exception text at ERROR, so the store/read broad excepts are load-bearing for secrecy (both are pinned)
findings.evidence: In mutant S17 (store re-raises), the log showed `ERROR app.middleware.error_handler:error_handler.py:240 Unhandled APIError: {... 'details': 'Failing row contains (B3BSENTINEL...`. A PostgREST row error would therefore put the refresh token in the Railway log if the store ever let it escape. S17 and S24 are both KILLED (R9 upsert-raises, R15). This handler is pre-existing code that the unit did not touch.
findings.fix: None for this unit. Keep R9[upsert-raises] and R15 frozen.

probes_run:
Results that came out clean:
- **Key handling and logs:** the private key never reaches a log, an exception message or the config repr. Every [SIWA] line is INFO or WARNING, carries no exc_info, and its arguments are int or str. 59 sentinels (authorization code, refresh, access and id tokens, sub, Apple error body, PEM lines, team and key ids, every client_secret seen) had 0 hits across ALL loggers, httpx and httpcore DEBUG included.
- **Client secret:** the header is exactly {alg ES256, kid} with no typ. Claims are exactly iss/iat/exp/aud/sub, exp - iat = 300, the signature is 64 bytes and verifies, and the secret is fresh per call.
- **Token at rest (044):** RLS is on with no policy; REVOKE ALL removes PUBLIC, anon and authenticated; exactly one GRANT (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE) goes to service_role; there is no anon grant. All of it is pinned (S12, S13, S14, S20 killed).
- **Timeouts and retries:** every Apple call is bounded in total (6 s per call, 12 s for a deletion, measured with a real transport). The exchange is single shot and the revoke makes at most 2 attempts.
- **Other checks:** CREDENTIALS_UNSET carries the key (S15 killed). The test file binds only low-entropy words to token-named names. gitleaks is clean. In app/ the bundle id appears only as the exact com.qaren.app, and only in CLAUDE.md. No failure probed blocks account deletion.
- **OpenAPI:** the authorization_code property ships unflagged, which is a stated limit in CLAUDE.md. /docs and /redoc are off on Railway (main.py:91-92).

Probes, in run order:
1. **gitleaks 8.30.1, range b965c63b..e8f11873** (git mode, no network, 13:40:11-13:40:23):
   - repo `.gitleaks.toml`: `INF no leaks found` rc=0;
   - default rules: `INF no leaks found` rc=0.
2. **AST literal scan** of the test files and the module (plain python, no pytest). The only literals bound to token/secret/key names are low-entropy words ('sess-a', 'sess-r', 'acc-x', 'idt', 'not-a-jwt', 'x', '', 'word', 'header.payload.signature') plus `TOKEN_URL` = the Apple URL. The module has 0 hits.
3. **Diff sweep, counts only**, over the 1891 added lines:
   - 0 each: PEM private header, sk-, JWT, credentialed URL, gmail, phone, qaren.app other than the bundle id, 10-char team-id shape;
   - bundle-like strings: `com.example.b3b` (synthetic, test file) and `com.qaren.app` (CLAUDE.md only; none under app/).
4. **Code reads:**
   - error_handler.validation_exception_handler logs nothing and does not echo the body;
   - sentry_service: include_local_variables=False (:681), max_request_body_size="never" (:684), LoggingIntegration(level=ERROR) (:651);
   - logging_config sets httpx to WARNING (:47);
   - no middleware reads or logs request bodies;
   - CREDENTIALS_UNSET is not referenced by app/;
   - main.py turns docs_url and redoc_url off on Railway (:91-92).
5. **Probe A**, plain python importing only app.services.apple_siwa_service (stdlib, httpx, jwt; no dotenv; only network is 127.0.0.1 servers owned by the probe). [py] probe_a 13:43:49-13:46:04 rc=0; rerun probe_a2 13:46:32-13:48:45 rc=0.
   - Secret shape all True: header {alg,kid}, claim keys, iss/sub/aud, exp-iat=300, iat~now, signature 64 B, fresh secret per call (`_now` +301).
   - 17 key forms: str / repr / args / context carry 0 key material (0 LEAK).
   - Attempt counts:
     - exchange: 1 on every failure; a hang ends at 6.02s;
     - revoke: 200:1, 400:1, 401:1, 500->200:2, 503x2:2, 429x2:2, ConnectError x3:2, RuntimeError:1, OSError:1;
     - revoke hang at the real `_CALL_DEADLINE`: 12.01s, 2 attempts.
   - Loopback, real AsyncHTTPTransport:
     - slow-drip body: 12.0s (TimeoutError x2);
     - slow-drip headers: 12.0s;
     - silent server: 10.47s (ReadTimeout x2).
   - Log capture:
     - [SIWA] records: 33, levels INFO and WARNING only, exc_info 0, argument types int and str;
     - `5_sentinel_hit_count: 0` of 59 sentinels across every logger (app, httpx, httpcore.connection, httpcore.http11 at DEBUG, asyncio).
6. **Probe B**, 30 nodes through the bounded runner. It reused the frozen RED harness (autouse env, network guard, fakes), ran as a temporary tests/test_zz_adv_b3b_sec_probe.py, and was deleted afterwards. [pyt] tag=b3b-adv-sec-probeB start=2026-10-17 13:51:40 end=2026-10-17 13:52:04 elapsed=24s bound=600s status=OK rc=0. 30 passed; [hermeticity] sentinel checked 30; [netguard] blocked 0.

   - P7: three 422 shapes: echo=False, logged=False.
